Dealer Selling New Chevy Corvette ZR1, Markup Will Leave You Speechless
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec
Can you believe it’s been almost two and a half years since Chevrolet pulled the wraps off the all-new ZR1 version of the C8-generation Corvette?
Well, the model premiered in mid-2024, boasting more oomph than the original Bugatti Veyron. The latter model is considered the world’s first hypercar, and its famous W16 engine with quad turbocharging was officially rated at 987 hp (1,001 ps/736 kW). The 8.0-liter unit, which was paired with a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and all-wheel drive, rocketed it to 60 mph (97 kph) in roughly 2.5 seconds, which was definitely a jaw-dropping achievement for something that hit the assembly line in 2005.
By comparison, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 is some two-tenths of a second faster, while costing a fraction of the price. More on the Benjamins in a few moments, as first, we have to remind you that the American hypercar has 1,064 horsepower to play with. This comes out to 1,079 metric horsepower and 794 kilowatts. The peak thrust is officially rated at 828 pound-feet (1,123 Nm), and power comes from the Z06’s engine, which has been equipped with two turbochargers in this case.
Chevy’s modern-day Corvette ZR1 can complete the standing quarter mile in 9.6 seconds at 150 mph (241 kph), the spec sheet reveals, and if you keep the right pedal pinned to the floor, then it will eventually top out at 233 mph (375 kph). If you want quicker sprints, then you may want to opt for the ZR1X version of the car. The top speed may be identical to the ZR1, but the 0-60 mph acceleration is dealt with in a whopping 1.89 seconds. This model takes 8.99 seconds to run the standing 1/4 mile at 157 mph (253 kph).
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec As for the firepower, it too features the same 5.5-liter V8 with twin turbocharging. However, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X also boasts electric assistance sourced from the E-Ray that is now dead and buried. In total, you are looking at a neck-snapping 1,250 bhp. That’s 1,268 horses for the metric crowd and 933 kilowatts. The powertrain develops 937 pound-feet (1,270 Nm) of torque in total. This means that the ZR1X can give modern-day supercars a real run for their money.
Speaking of the finances, a brand new Chevy Corvette ZR1X from the 2027 model year will set you back a minimum of $227,800. This means that it is a lot more affordable than the Lamborghini Temerario, not to mention a heck of a lot faster. In fact, it can beat the larger, punchier, and more expensive Revuelto, too. Well, at least in a straight-line acceleration, according to the spec sheet.
However, we wish you good luck if you want to buy one for a little over the MSRP, because you’d have more chances of finding a needle in a haystack due to the insane markups. The same goes for the Chevy Corvette ZR1 , which officially starts at $198,000 for the latest model year, the bowtie brand’s official US website reveals.
On average, the 2025 to 2027 model year cars tend to fetch between just under @250,000 and over $320,000 in today’s used car market. The latter sum is obviously reserved for barely driven examples from the latest model year, which feature plenty of optional extras, such as the ZTK Track Pack, and the former will get you an earlier model year that has seen some action and does not pack that may goodies.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec The pictured Chevy Corvette ZR1 is looking for a new home as we speak. The selling dealer behind it, which is known as @limitedspec on Instagram, has not revealed the model year. However, it did reveal that this machine has only 360 miles (580 km) under its belt. Therefore, it a new ride, hence the ultra clean look inside and out, as you can see for yourselves in the images shared in the gallery.
This ride features a glossy black look on the outside, sits on black Y-spoke alloys that spin around the red brake calipers, and has a mostly red interior, albeit with a few black touches here and there for some contrast. Carbon trim is also on deck, alongside the familiar screen setup, a flat-bottom steering wheel with a red 12 o’clock marker, and no wall of buttons, to no one’s surprise, because that was a thing on the pre-facelifted C8.
Strangely, the dealer did not have much to say about this Chevy Corvette ZR1 , as you are about to see in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page. However, it did reveal that this American hypercar is located in Miami, Florida, and as you can imagine, it costs a lot of money. At the time of writing, the asking price was $299,980, which is actually more than the ZR1X’s MSRP.
Therefore, if you believe that this C8 ‘Vette is worth $300K, then you know what to do next, don’t you? But would you really fork out that much money for this ride? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Limited Spec Automotive (@limitedspec)
